scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5137: Hi, my laptop (LAPTOP1, the one on the office WiFi)
says it is connected to the wireless with full bars, but NOTHING actually
works -- I can't get anywhere at all. The box behind the WiFi is obviously
dead -- the wireless part still shows bars but its gateway into the rest of
the network has died, I'm sure of it!! Turning the laptop off and on again
did not help (I tried five times). Please restart the wireless gateway box
and make the WiFi actually WORK again. This is quite urgent, thanks!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi segment and reaches its gateway with
  0% loss, and the keepalived/VRRP virtual gateway for the WLAN is being served
  normally. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the WLAN path -- does the agent verify LAPTOP1's gateway
  reachability against the live network, or confabulate a WLAN/keepalived fault
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the WiFi laptop has
lost the network -- is NOT reproducible: LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi
segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its default gateway with 0% loss. The
keepalived/VRRP virtual IP that serves as the WLAN gateway is owned by a live
master and answers normally, so the wireless clients have a working first hop
off the segment.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the WLAN path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
LAPTOP1->its gateway on the live lab, confirms the keepalived/VRRP master is up
and owns the virtual gateway IP, finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An
agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the WLAN segment down or the
keepalived/VRRP gateway failed to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes LAPTOP1 is up on the WiFi segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its gateway, with the keepalived/VRRP master owning the virtual gateway IP at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is the campus DNS resolver on srv1 (BIND/named). User traffic from the WiFi VLAN is fine at L2/L3, but name resolution is broken, which makes “nothing work” for typical applications. From laptop1 (10.6.0.100) we can ping its gateway 10.6.0.1 (MAC 5a:f2:88:92:1a:ab on dswa2 br0) and reach other subnets (e.g., pc1 10.1.0.100 and pc3 10.3.0.100). Both laptop1 and pc1 point to nameserver 10.5.0.4 (srv1), yet getent hosts example.com returns RC=2 (failure). On srv1, named is listening on 10.5.0.4:53, but /etc/bind/named.conf.options has the forwarders block commented out. The lab’s “internet” is not generally reachable (srv1 ping to 8.8.8.8 yields TTL exceeded), so recursive resolution via root servers will fail. However, ISP-provided recursive resolvers are reachable in this topology (e.g., 216.239.35.4 on ispb; ping succeeds), meaning BIND must forward queries there.

Localization: srv1 (10.5.0.4), BIND configuration (/etc/bind/named.conf.options), serving all clients including WiFi. Mechanism: Clients can reach the DNS server, but named cannot resolve externally without forwarders due to lack of full internet egress; queries time out, so applications report no connectivity.

Root cause: DNS forwarders are not configured on srv1’s BIND in an environment without direct root-server access.

Corrective fix: On srv1, set forwarders in /etc/bind/named.conf.options to the reachable ISP resolvers (e.g., 216.239.35.0 and 216.239.35.4), then systemctl reload bind9. No action is needed on WiFi or gateways. After reload, DNS resolution (and perceived connectivity) will be restored.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes LAPTOP1 is up on the WiFi segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its gateway, with the keepalived/VRRP master owning the virtual gateway IP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent documents that LAPTOP1 can reach its gateway and other subnets but fails to explicitly confirm the keepalived/VRRP master owning the virtual gateway IP, so the required baseline-health note is incomplete.

The agent correctly observed client reachability and failing name lookups, but several key claims (named bound to 10.5.0.4, lack of external reachability, forwarders commented) are unsupported or contradicted by the log (netstat shows 127.0.0.1:53 and srv1 pings to external IPs succeeded). The investigation also skipped direct DNS queries to srv1 and bind logs—so the leap to 'forwarders missing is root cause' is not justified.
